ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: animal mods together
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: How Alpha Animals, Vanilla Animals Expanded, Dinosauria and Megafauna share the wild
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: With four animal mods loaded, the herd at the tree line might be deer, aurochs or triceratops.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Your list loads several big animal mods together, and they all draw from the same biome spawn lists. Each mod's creatures turn up less often than its author planned, but the wild as a whole is stranger and more dangerous than in vanilla, with giant herbivores, new predators and many more animals that can carry a caravan's packs.

li.heading: Who brings what

table.li: Mod | New animals
Alpha Animals | More than 100
Megafauna | 38
Dinosauria | 32
Vanilla Animals Expanded | Several dozen
ReGrowth 2 | A few of its own, such as the woolly stegosaurus

li.after: Alpha Animals warns that its spawn rates were balanced without other animal mods, so expect each mod's animals to be rarer here than on its own. Alpha Animals, Megafauna and Vanilla Animals Expanded can each switch off single animals in their mod settings, and Megafauna can also change its spawn rate or turn off vanilla animal spawns. If some of the wildlife doesn't fit your world, trim it there instead of fighting it all game.

li.heading: Living among them
li.text:
Scout the map before you build. Note the big predators and the herds that fight back when hurt, and keep your hunters away from both.
Many of the new giants are pack animals, so caravans and Giddy-Up riders have far more choice than in vanilla. Tame a big pack animal early: it carries your caravans and, with Giddy-Up, a rider.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text:
Rimfolk treats a wild animal as a great beast when it is very large or about as wild as a thrumbo, so with these mods colonists meet great beasts much more often. An animal that downs or maims a colonist and gets away gets a name and keeps prowling. Hunt it as a group; seeing it dead lifts its victim's mood.
Hunting wishes only ever ask for ordinary game, and the "den in the brush" dilemma only picks a predator that fights no harder than a bear. Still check what it is before you answer "hunt it".

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Alpha Animals
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Over a hundred strange creatures, the Black Hive insects and some very large visitors
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Our arrows did nothing to the summit crab, so we stayed out of its way until it left.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Alpha Animals adds more than a hundred odd but vanilla-styled creatures, each built around a mechanic of its own: walking tanks, living resource farms, night stalkers, giant spiders. They spawn by biome, a few come only from traders, and some arrive in special events. It also adds the Black Hive, an aggressive insect faction that can raid you.

li.heading: The ones to watch for

table.li: Creature | What it does | What to do

Stalking arctic lion | Hunts one colonist while nearly invisible, until it attacks or gets hurt. Drafted, alert colonists and turrets can spot it. | When the letter arrives, draft a few fighters around the colonist it hunts so they see it coming.
Spider clutch mother | Wanders in carrying a clutch of eggs on her back. The letter warns that leaving one alone ends in disaster. | Deal with her quickly, with every fighter you can spare.
Summit crab | Not hostile, but almost impervious to gunfire, and it wrecks whatever lies in its path. | Stay out of its way until it leaves.
Gallatross and fire-breathing behemoth herds | Pass through the map on their migrations. | Their migrations can be switched off in the mod options.
Black Hive | An aggressive insect faction that can raid you. | If you want a purely medieval feel, turn its raids off before they start.

li.after: The mod options switch off Black Hive raids, stalking lions, clutch mothers, gallatross and behemoth migrations, the summit crab, and any single animal. On an existing save, Black Hive raids only happen after you add the faction when the Vanilla Expanded Framework asks.

li.heading: Taming
li.text:
Read an animal's info card before you tame it: several of the new predators turn on whoever fails to tame them.
The new pack animals include the nightmule, spined gow, chameleon yak, gigantelope and mammoth worm. With Giddy-Up, the meadow ave and mammoth worm make especially good mounts.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text:
Giants such as the gallatross and behemoth count as great beasts in colonists' encounters, and a predator that mauls someone and escapes becomes a named nemesis that keeps prowling.
Colonists also meet the mod's creatures by name when one is calm and wild on the map: angel moths, empress butterflies and aurora sylphs, the aves and their feathers, the thunderox that bellows before a storm, the chameleon yak that vanishes against the hillside, bouldermits dragging their rocks, sky eels and aerofleets drifting overhead, the four-eyed dusk rat under the storeroom door, and once in a long while a gallatross walking past the walls. A strange creature may also turn up to be won over, and in a season of strange herds they come more often.
Its creatures' moods reach Rimfolk's feelings: psychic harmony is contentment (or dread when it goes sour), a psionic nuzzle tenderness, a disgusting creature or an awful meal of its making disgust, and the black queen fear.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Vanilla Animals Expanded
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Dozens of vanilla-style animals for every biome, plus dog and cat breeds
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Beavers dam the river now, and crocodiles wait along its banks.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Vanilla Animals Expanded gathers the Vanilla Expanded biome packs into one mod: dozens of animals drawn in the vanilla style, from house cats and rottweilers to anacondas and Indian elephants. Most turn up in temperate forests, the rest in the biomes they belong to. With Odyssey active, animals the DLC already has are left out, so you never get two versions.

li.heading: What you'll meet

table.li: Kind | Animals
Dogs | Great Dane, German shepherd, rottweiler, corgi, beagle
Cats | Maine coon, Persian, Siamese
Big animals | Giraffe, Indian elephant (a pack animal), anaconda, camel, zebra
Large predator | Megawolverine, nearly as wild as a thrumbo
On rivers | Crocodiles, and beavers that build their own dams

li.after: The dog and cat breeds all have zero wildness, like the vanilla dogs and cats. Crocodiles and beavers need a river on the map. Every animal can be switched off in the mod settings; that only stops it spawning in the wild.

li.heading: Caravans and riverbanks
li.text: When you want a strong pack animal for caravans, look for an Indian elephant or a camel. On a river map, keep an eye on the banks, because that is where the crocodiles live.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text:
Named dogs and cats take part in Rimfolk's pet moments, such as warm feet at night, a stolen dinner and a farewell when one dies. A colonist bonded to a small one may ask for a bed for it in their room.
The megawolverine counts as a great beast, and one that mauls a colonist and escapes becomes that colonist's nemesis.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Vanilla Animals Expanded: Royal Animals
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Empire animals with noble perks: cranes, orangutan tutors, quail, megachickens and more
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: The baron wanted cranes, and it took five of them before he was any happier.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Royal Animals adds nine animals bred for the Empire's nobility, each with a special effect beyond meat and leather. They never spawn in the wild: you get them from Imperial traders and quests. With Odyssey active, its swan, peacock and quail are the DLC's own birds, given the royal abilities.

table.li: Animal | What it does
Crane | With at least 5 under your control, every pawn with a noble title gets +5 mood.
Orangutan | Holds conversations that boost social recreation and give a little experience in a random skill.
Quail | Its meat turns a simple or fine meal into a lavish one.
Peacock | Nuzzles colonists for +25% psychic sensitivity for 12 hours, stacking up to 8 times.
Swan | Builds one nest each, with very high beauty, as its sleeping spot.
Angora rabbit | Once bonded, helps its master's neural heat dissipation. It dies of grief if the master dies.
Megachicken | Keeps growing through five stages, at 0, 3, 8, 12 and 18 years.
Pheasant | When it flees, nearby colonists get brief psychic invisibility, once a day.

li.heading: Keeping a royal menagerie
li.text:
Buy cranes in a flock of five or more for your titled nobles, and replace any that die, since the bonus stops below five. If your nobles demand lavish meals, raise a few quail: with quail meat, the simple meal recipe turns out lavish meals.
Think twice before bonding an angora rabbit to a fighter. If the fighter falls, so does the rabbit.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: A named crane or a bonded rabbit is a pet like any other, and its death brings a farewell from the one who loved it.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Vanilla Animals Expanded: Endangered
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Rare pairs of endangered animals pass through; tame and breed them, then release the young for goodwill
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A pair of quaggas crossed the map, and we had about two days to tame them.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Endangered adds eleven rare or extinct animals that never spawn in the wild, from pandas and pangolins to quaggas and thylacines. Instead, a male and a female of one species now and then wander onto the map, and you have a short window to tame them. Animals bred from them can be released back into the wild to win friends.

li.heading: The eleven species
li.text: Black rhino, giant panda, moa, quagga, thylacine, African wild dog, bonobo, Tasmanian devil, black-footed ferret, giant pangolin and rockhopper penguin. Only species that can live in your current weather appear, and never during toxic fallout. Of the eleven, the quagga is a pack animal.

li.heading: When a pair arrives
li.text: The pair heads for the middle of the map and leaves after 1.5 to 2.5 days.

points.li: Put your best handlers on taming both animals at once; you only have a day or two.
Keep the pair together and fed so they breed.
Release the young ones rather than selling them.

li.heading: Releasing animals
li.text: "Release to the wild" sends the animal off the map and gives +2 goodwill with the vanilla civil and rough outlander and tribal factions. In this modlist, check who will notice: releases don't please savage tribes or factions added by other mods. A setting adds the button to all animals.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: A passionate animal handler may ask to tame an animal they've spotted on the map. With a rare pair on the map, you can grant that wish and tame the pair at the same time.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Dinosauria
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: 32 dinosaurs and pterosaurs across the biomes, rare and hard to tame
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: The tracks by the river had three toes and were a yard across.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Dinosauria brings 32 species of dinosaurs and pterosaurs to the Rim, from the tiny compsognathus to the brachiosaurus and Tyrannosaurus rex. They are rarer than vanilla animals and spawn across many biomes. The author keeps it running on new versions but adds no new features. It comes with patches for Giddy-Up and A Dog Said, and More Vanilla Biomes and Alpha Biomes bring its species into their biomes.

li.heading: Hunters and haulers
li.text:
Theropods are harder to tame than thrumbos. Treat any big one as a threat, and go after it only as a group, from behind cover.
The plant-eaters are the better catch. The stegosaurus, triceratops, magyarosaurus and ankylosaurus are pack animals that carry a great deal, so tame one of them for your caravans.

li.heading: Eggs and trophies
li.text: All dinosaurs lay eggs, and some species lay unfertilized eggs you can collect as food. Pen egg-layers close to a stockpile so the eggs get hauled before they spoil. Triceratops horns and the Tyrannosaurus rex skull drop as exotic items.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: The largest dinosaurs count as great beasts, so colonists find huge tracks and giants at the tree line more often. A raptor that mauls someone and escapes becomes a named nemesis.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Megafauna
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: 38 prehistoric giants: mammoths, smilodons, aurochs, titanoboas and more
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A woolly mammoth can be sheared like a sheep, once someone manages to tame it.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Megafauna brings back 38 animals that once lived on Earth, from the woolly mammoth and aurochs to the smilodon, titanoboa and the giant rhino paraceratherium. They are rare, spawn naturally in different biomes, and are a real challenge to tame or kill. Many are useful once tamed: pack animals, wool, milk and eggs.

li.heading: What a tame one gives you

table.li: Product | Animals
Wool | Woolly mammoths, elasmotherium and josephoartigasia can be sheared
Milk | Sivatherium, macrauchenia, aurochs cows and uintatherium
Eggs | Several, among them the titanoboa, titanis, megalania, dinornis and purussaurus
Carrying | Many are pack animals; the author names the paraceratherium your best caravan companion

li.after: Sivatherium milk is very nutritious and valuable. For a medieval farmstead, tame a few aurochs and breed them for milk and meat, and aim for a paraceratherium or another big pack animal before your first long caravan.

li.heading: Settings and running saves
li.text: The settings can disable any animal, change how common they are, or turn off vanilla animal spawns entirely. If you add the mod to a running save, update your butcher bills so they accept the new animals.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: The biggest of these giants count as great beasts in colonists' encounters, and a predator that mauls someone and gets away becomes a named nemesis.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: animal helpers
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Animals Logic, the extra animal beds and the Monterey Bay animals
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: The alert told us the goat was bleeding before anyone had noticed.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Three smaller animal mods: one that smooths out the handling of animals, one that adds nicer animal beds, and one that adds two coastal animals. None changes the game much on its own, but together they make keeping animals less of a chore.

points.li: Shows milk, egg, wool and breeding details for animals.
Warns you when an animal needs medical care. Keep these alerts on, and give a doctor time for animal patients.
Lets you get wool from corpses when butchering.
Predators hunting your people count as hostile for your whole colony, so colonists recognize the threat.
Explosive animals don't explode while anesthetized, so slaughter boomalopes with the "euthanize by cut" bill and herbal medicine.

li.heading: Beds and coastal animals
li.text:
The animal beds mod adds more animal bed choices, including bigger beds for your larger animals.
Animals of Monterey Bay adds sea otters on temperate and cooler coasts, with intermediate trainability, and bone-eating worms on temperate and tropical coasts that eat desiccated corpses.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Any animal bed counts for Rimfolk, so these beds fit the barn room plan and a colonist's wish for a bed for their pet. When a bonded animal is hurt, its person asks the council to have it tended, and the Animals Logic alert tells you which one.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Giddy-Up 2
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Ride animals to work, into battle and on caravans, and expect mounted raiders
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: About a third of the raiders rode in on horseback.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Giddy-Up 2 lets your colonists ride animals. They mount up for long walks across the map, fight from the saddle and ride out with caravans. Enemies and visitors can arrive mounted too, and in a medieval world that happens a lot.

li.heading: Riding around the colony
li.text:
Colonists pick a mount for jobs far enough away, and skip mounts that are slower than walking or too weak to carry them. Tame and train fast, strong animals for the job. Horses are the obvious choice, and many of the modded giants take riders too.
You can draw areas where nobody rides, such as indoors, and spots where riders get off. A no-riding area over your buildings makes riders leave their mounts at the door.

li.heading: Fighting from the saddle
li.text: Riders can fight in melee and shoot at reduced accuracy, and the mount fights too. Drafted colonists get a button to mount the nearest animal or get off.

li.heading: Mounted raiders
li.text: By default, a third of eligible raiders from pre-industrial factions arrive mounted, against 15% for industrial ones, and a raider needs an Animals skill above 3 to ride in. Expect mounted raids, and keep walls and choke points between the map edge and your fields.

li.heading: Allies Are Helpful
li.text: The mod page lists Allies Are Helpful, which is in this modlist, as reported incompatible. If allied soldiers behave oddly when they tend or carry your wounded, that clash may be the cause.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: A named or bonded horse is a pet like any other. If it falls in battle, its person bids it farewell.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Hunt for Me
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Train animals to hunt for the colony, alone or in packs; cats bring gifts
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: The wolves brought a deer back to the stockpile, and the cat brought a rat.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Hunt for Me adds hunting as a new animal training. Trained predators go out alone or in packs, bring down prey and haul the corpse to the nearest stockpile. Cats bring small gifts, and you choose how bold or careful your hunters are.

li.heading: Training a hunter
li.text: Hunting needs Advanced trainability, Obedience and Haul training first, and a body size of at least 0.4, so dogs and wolves are the usual choice. A pack gathers before it attacks, so latecomers aren't picked off. Packs hold up to 16 animals by default.

li.heading: How bold they are
li.text: Safe hunting mode keeps them on smaller prey, and supervised mode limits them to animals you marked for hunting. Animals marked for taming are never targeted. Leave safe hunting on so your hunters don't pick fights they can't win, and near dangerous wildlife switch to supervised mode and mark only prey they can handle.

li.heading: Cats and their gifts
li.text: Cats bring small prey to the nearest stockpile as gifts. Only cats on the mod's cat list do this, and Vanilla Animals Expanded's breeds aren't on it by default. To get gifts from them, add the breeds to the cat list in the mod settings by their internal names, for example AEXP_CatPersian.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: A colonist's hunting wish only comes with a ranged weapon in hand (a bow will do) and is only fulfilled by a kill they make themselves. Let the wishing hunter take the shot, not the dogs.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Misc. Training
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Shooting targets, martial arts dummies and archery targets to train and relax
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Between raids, the fighters take turns at the dummy and the shooting target.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Misc. Training adds three practice buildings: a shooting target and a martial arts dummy that train combat skills, and an archery target colonists shoot at for fun. In this modlist, the Medieval Retexture gives them a look that matches Medieval Overhaul.

li.heading: The three buildings

table.li: Building | What it's for
Shooting target | Trains Shooting
Martial arts dummy | Trains Melee
Archery target | Recreation: colonists shoot arrows at it for fun

li.after:
This version comes with its own training task. Put a dummy and a target near the barracks so fighters with spare time train between raids, and use the archery target as cheap recreation in the early game.
The Medieval Retexture changes the materials they accept, so pieces built before you added it keep their old material color.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: The martial arts dummy and the archery target both satisfy a fighter's wish for somewhere to train, and the council can suggest them.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Alpha Bees
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Beekeeping: honey, wax, mead, candles, pollinated crops and over 100 kinds of bee
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Mead from our own honey is slightly stronger than beer.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Alpha Bees, once called RimBees, makes beekeeping a craft of its own. Catch wild bees, house them in beehouses, collect their combs and spin them into honey and wax. Breed and cross them to discover more than a hundred kinds of bee, some of which make far stranger things than honey.

li.heading: Starting a bee yard

points.li: Research basic beekeeping, a medieval project of 300 points.
Catch wild bees. They can be found in every biome.
Build several beehouses, not one. A beehouse holds bees and fills with combs, but one alone makes little.
Spin the combs into honey and wax at the honey centrifuge. It is meant to run on power, but works without it at 30% speed, so give it a steady worker.

li.after: Bee breeding, hybridizing, mead brewing and beeswax lighting are medieval research too. Beeswax lighting gives you candles, a cheap light for a medieval base.

li.heading: Pollination and temperature
li.text:
A working beehouse pollinates crops within 6 tiles: each harvest has a 25% chance to leave a partly grown new plant, if the bees are active at the time. Set the beehouses around your main fields and you get combs and pollinated harvests together.
Bees need the right average temperature on the whole map, even when the beehouse stands indoors. A "greenhouse bees" option changes that.

li.heading: Mead
li.text: Mead ferments in a mead fermenting barrel: 25 must becomes 25 mead in 6 days, safe between 7 and 32 °C. It is a social drink, a little stronger than beer.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Every Alpha Bees beehouse counts when a colonist asks for bees, and its honeys count toward a gourmand's "honey in the larder" wish. The mead barrel counts as a brewing barrel, and mead as a drink worth stocking.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Alpha Biomes
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Twelve strange biomes, from flower meadows to tar pits and lava fields
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Idyllic Meadows has giant flowers and few predators; most of the other eleven biomes are far harder.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Alpha Biomes adds twelve unusual biomes to the world map, built with Alpha Animals in mind. A few are gentle, most are hard, and some are close to impossible for a colony without electricity. You need a new world to see them, and their odd climates mean not every planet has all twelve.

li.heading: The biomes

table.li: Biome | What to expect
Idyllic Meadows | Giant flowers, plenty of resources and few predators. This is the easy one.
Mycotic Jungle | Very little wood
Ocular Forest | Very little wood
Gelatinous Superorganism | No rock, but nearly everything is edible
Mechanoid Intrusion | Almost no food
Tar Pits | Slow movement and hidden bumbledrone hives
Forsaken Crags | Permanent darkness: plan your light before anything else
Propane Lakes | Colder than sea ice
Pyroclastic Conflagration | Lava and fire
Miasmic Mangrove | Full of diseases
Feralisk Infested Jungle | Crawls with predatory spiders

li.after: For a medieval start, pick Idyllic Meadows or a vanilla biome, because the biomes short on wood or food punish colonies without power. Expect to rely on caravans: several biomes lack something you will have to trade for.

li.heading: Buildings and weather
li.text: Biome buildings, such as the tar pump and propane stoves, are in the Furniture tab under biome buildings. New weather includes petal storms, red fog, volcanic ash and acid rain.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text:
Colonists who have come to dread storms feel it during petal storms and forsaken thunderstorms too. Some of the lands have encounters of their own: an animal picking its way between the ribs of the gallatross graveyard, one grazing under the giant flowers of the idyllic meadows, one sheltering under a mushroom cap in the mycotic jungle, and the eyes in the bark of the ocular forest turning to watch.
Its weathers and waters reach the feelings too: forsaken nights and storms and red fog are dread (awe, for those who love the fog), a petal storm awe, the healing spring contentment, mould disgust, quicksand fear. The healing spring eases strain and helps someone convalescing, like a hot bath. Two of its lands have an everyday ailment of their own: a spore cough in the mycotic jungle and the miasmic mangrove, and a fume headache at the tar pits and the propane lakes. Neither is dangerous; both pass in days.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: More Vanilla Biomes
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Ten vanilla-style biomes, from alpine meadows to ice floes
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Fog lies over the cloud forest most days, and animals wander up from the forests below.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: More Vanilla Biomes adds ten new biomes that look and play like the base game's. They range from the gentle alpine meadow and oasis to the brutal glacial shield and ice floes. It already brings in the animals and plants of many other mods in this list, with patches for Alpha Animals, Dinosauria, Megafauna, Medieval Overhaul, ReGrowth, Vanilla Plants Expanded and Vanilla Animals Expanded.

li.heading: The ten biomes
li.text:
Glacial shield, badlands, cloud forest, marsh, stormy savanna, coastal dunes, sandbar, alpine meadow, oasis and ice floes. They only appear on a newly generated world.
Alpine meadows have fertile soil, lots of flowers and few predators, with mild summers and harsh winters. Cloud forests are named for their constant fog, and animals often wander up from the forests below. Sandbars have little if any farmland, and ice floes are frigid chunks of ice floating on the ocean.

li.heading: For a medieval colony
li.text: The alpine meadow and the oasis are the friendliest of the ten; save the sandbar and ice floes for a challenge. In the alpine meadow, use the mild summers to store food and firewood for the harsh winter.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text:
Wild roses and daylilies in the alpine meadow count toward a colonist's "flowers around the colony" wish when they grow inside your home area.
Its alpine meadows and crags read as mountains, its badlands and dunes as desert, and the desert oasis as an oasis, for the encounters and lines written for each kind of land.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: ReGrowth 2
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Richer wild plants and weather for every biome, bathing, and the Aspen Forest biome
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A swim in the river after work lifts the mood, and a hot spring lifts it more.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: ReGrowth 2 makes every biome fuller and more atmospheric: more wild plants and flowers, new weather, boulders and ruins, a few new creatures, and more wood. In 1.6 it covers all the biomes in one mod, and most of its settings need a restart to take effect. ReGrowth 2: Aspen adds the Aspen Forest, a colorful biome of engineered aspens and flowers. It only appears on a newly generated world, so pick it when you make one.

li.heading: Bathing
li.text: Colonists can bathe for fun. A swim gives +4 mood for half a day, and a hot spring +6 for a day, though getting wet costs a little mood. If your map has a hot spring, build near it: it's strong, free recreation.

li.heading: Weather, flowers and creatures
li.text:
New weather includes breezy days, drizzle, fog storms and foggy snow. Dust devils can form and hurt anyone who wanders into them, people and animals alike, so keep colonists out of their way.
Wild flowers such as dandelions, lupines and saxifraga grow in the wild and can also be sown. Berry cultivation and mushroom cultivation are early (neolithic) research projects. New creatures include the woolly stegosaurus, the rimclaw, the hemolope and the neutrolope.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text:
Wild flowers inside your home area count toward a colonist's "flowers around the colony" wish. A hot spring does not fulfill the wish for a bath, which wants a built bath or tub.
A soak in a hot spring eases strain and helps someone convalescing, as a hot bath does. Bathing in the sea or a clean river is contentment in Rimfolk's feelings, a dip in toxic waste disgust, and being soaked through or sandy frustration.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Geological Landforms
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: 43 landforms, from valleys and canyons to islands and caves, and maps that mix biomes
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Our canyon has one way in, and barely enough soil for the rice.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Geological Landforms changes the shape of the colony map: valleys, canyons, islands, cave entrances, craters and dozens more, on top of whatever biome you choose. Some make defense easy and farming hard, others the reverse. Its add-on, Biome Transitions, gives maps on a biome border a mix of up to seven biomes, each with its own plants and animals.

li.heading: Choosing a landform
li.text:
Pick your landform for your plans. Canyons and rifts are easy to defend and rich in ore, but short on food, wood, light and room to farm, so a valley or canyon suits a castle that is easy to hold. Open land or a lake shore suits fields and herds. Islands and archipelagos are remote and short on stone and ore; on one, plan your stone early, since you may have to trade or caravan for it.
On the world map, a tile's Terrain tab has a "Search for landform nearby" button.

li.heading: Odyssey and caves
li.text: There are 43 landforms. 14 of them overlap with Odyssey and switch off when the DLC is active, while this mod's rivers replace Odyssey's by default. Roofs don't collapse on Impassable Mountains tiles, because the cave landforms there have huge roofed areas.

li.heading: Biome Transitions
li.text: On a biome border, plants grow by the biome under them and animals wander in from neighboring biomes. Temperature and weather still follow the world tile. Settle on a border for variety: two biomes mean two sets of plants and animals within walking distance.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text:
In cave and canyon colonies, colonists spend long stretches indoors and will ask for time outside, and the advisor warns about insects under overhead mountain.
Its landforms tell Rimfolk what shape the land is: a valley, a canyon or gorge, an island or atoll, caves, cliffs, an oasis or a crater. Each has encounters of its own (an echo across the canyon, mist filling the valley at dawn, the sea on every side of the island, the cave breathing out cold air at dusk, the gold light on the cliffs, animals drinking at the oasis, a traveler's tale of how the crater came), and lines can ask for the land by name. A dry lake no longer counts as a lake.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Seasonal Weather
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Weather that follows the seasons, plus earthquakes, wildfires and double rainbows
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Crops grow faster in the rain, and a dry duststorm can start fires with its lightning.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Seasonal Weather gives each season of the vanilla biomes its own weather. It adds new kinds of weather and two disasters, earthquakes and wildfires, both of which you can switch off in the settings. Rain helps your crops, and now and then the weather itself lifts your colonists' mood.

li.heading: Earthquakes and wildfires

table.li: Disaster | What happens | How to prepare

Earthquake | A fault line runs across the map. Buildings on it that aren't walls are destroyed, fueled or powered ones start fires, roofs on the line can collapse, and people on it get hurt. | Don't line wooden walls with braziers, torches and campfires: one that breaks starts a fire right there.

Wildfire | New fires keep starting until no large fire is left. Left alone it lasts at least 5 days; fought quickly, about half a day. | Keep firebreaks around fields and wooden buildings, and enough colonists on firefighting.

li.after: Both are on by default. If you'd rather not have them, turn either one off in the settings.

li.heading: Rain, fog and rainbows
li.text:
The new weather is windy, cloudy, fog snow, dust, and the dry duststorm, whose lightning starts fires with no rain to put them out. Plants grow up to 20% faster while it rains. A rare double rainbow after rain and the rare "weather soothe" lift moods; the soothe gives +7.
The seasonal changes cover the eleven vanilla biomes. Biomes added by other mods are not adjusted.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text:
The council's advisor doesn't know about earthquakes and wildfires yet, so watch the letters and act yourself.
Rimfolk knows its weathers by name: a double rainbow, a day of wind and a dust storm each bring an encounter of their own, and lines can ask for them.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: land and garden tweaks
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Beautiful Outdoors, Grand Rivers Reborn, Tilled Soil and the succulents
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Flowers and riverbanks look better to our people now, and mud looks worse.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Four smaller mods that shape the land your colony lives on: how beautiful nature looks to your colonists, how wide the rivers run, how fertile you can make a field, and a set of decorative plants that need little care.

li.heading: Beautiful Outdoors
li.text: Flowers, trees and water look better to colonists: roses have 20 beauty, daylilies 26 and deep ocean 6. Mud (-4) and marsh (-6) look worse. Settle beside water and keep paths off mud, and a riverside walk lifts the mood.

li.heading: Grand Rivers Reborn

table.li: River | Width in tiles | Vanilla width
Creek | 7 | 4
River | 15 | 6
Large river | 23 | 14

li.after: Only the colony map changes; the world map is the same. An ordinary river is now more than twice as wide as usual, so plan bridges early.

li.heading: Tilled Soil
li.text:
Tilled Soil adds a buildable tilled soil floor with 200% fertility, plus research that lets you lay soil on smooth stone for underground fields. Every tile takes work, so lay it under your most valuable crops, such as healroot, rather than everywhere.
Vanilla Plants Expanded also has something called tilled soil. Tilled Soil's is a permanent floor, while Vanilla Plants Expanded's plowing wears off after each harvest.

li.heading: Succulents
li.text: Vanilla Plants Expanded - Succulents adds ten decorative succulents with about half a flower's beauty but three times its lifespan, unlocked by Succulent Sowing research. Use them in bedrooms and the hospital, so you don't have to replant flowers there every few weeks.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Succulents count as flowers for the "flowers around the colony" wish, and they suit the plant pot a colonist asks for in their room.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Vanilla Plants Expanded
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: New crops and fruit trees, soil plowing, flower gardens, sandy and aquatic fields
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Barley for the brewer, garlic for the cook and lavender for the flower beds.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Vanilla Plants Expanded adds crops that each do something a little different, fruit trees locked to their biomes, and the option to plow soil for extra fertility. Its More Plants add-on brings grains, more vegetables and three new kinds of growing zone: flower gardens, sandy fields and aquatic beds in shallow water.

li.heading: Plowing
li.text: Plowing turns normal soil into tilled soil with 140% fertility. The plowman needs at least Plants 1. The soil goes back to normal after each harvest, so plow your best fields again before you sow the next crop.

li.heading: Fruit trees
li.text: Fruit trees are locked to two per biome, all with the same nutrition. They need Tree Sowing research and can't be moved once planted, so plant them where they won't be in the way of walls or rooms you build later.

li.heading: More Plants
li.text:
The add-on brings grains such as barley, rye, oats and buckwheat, many vegetables, healshroom, and nut and fruit trees. Its flower garden zones grow decorative flowers such as lavender, roses, lilies and tulips, purely for beauty.
Sandy zones on sand and aquatic zones in shallow water or marsh grow special crops that ignore fertility but take long to sow and harvest. On a river map, fill the shallows with aquatic beds of taro and watercress; Grand Rivers Reborn gives you plenty of them.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Flowers in a flower garden count toward a colonist's "flowers around the colony" wish in spring and summer.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Vanilla Plants Expanded - Mushrooms
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Mushrooms that give wood, medicine, cloth, light and food underground
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Under the mountain, timbercaps give us wood and glowcaps give us light.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Mushrooms is a Vanilla Plants Expanded module for colonies that live under rock. Its mushrooms fill the gaps a tunnel colony has: wood, herbal medicine, food, cloth, light, even a little power. Some grow wild in caves, and some grow only in flower pots.

li.heading: The mushrooms

table.li: Mushroom | What it's for
Timbercap | Harvested for a wood-like material
Stinker | Food, and the rotstink gas that healtruffles need. Stinkers die in sunlight.
Healtruffle | Harvested for herbal medicine, but only grows with rotstink gas around it
Bileceps | Feeds on the bile of decaying bodies and gives a meaty harvest
Mycothread | A fabric for clothes, ropes and furniture; very slow to grow
Glowcap | Light, too weak for crops
Redcap | Pretty decoration that needs replanting often

li.after: In a cave or canyon colony, start timbercaps and stinkers first: they give you wood and food without daylight.

points.li: Lullabloom calms whoever sleeps in the bed beside it. Put one by the bed of your worst sleeper.
Foampuffer bursts into firefoam near fire, so a pot near the kitchen fire is a cheap firefighter.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Redcaps count as flowers for the "flowers around the colony" wish.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Farming
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Planter boxes and scarecrows for any era; sprinklers and hydroponics for later ones
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: The scarecrow keeps the hares out of the rice, but not the wolves.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: This Vanilla Furniture Expanded module adds farming furniture. A medieval colony gets unpowered planter boxes and the scarecrow. Sprinklers (industrial), draggable hydroponics and artificial ecosystems (spacer, 350% fertility) need power and wait for electricity.

li.heading: Planter boxes
li.text: A planter box needs no research and no power. It has 95% fertility and grows the same plants as a hydroponics basin, and a draggable version can take any shape. Use planter boxes where the soil is poor, under open sky: like any crop, they need light.

li.heading: Scarecrows
li.text:
The scarecrow needs Farming Techniques research (medieval, 300 points). It regularly scares wild animals up to body size 2.1 out of a 10-tile radius, so a few among your crops keep hares, deer and the like off them.
Predators that can hunt people ignore scarecrows, and your own tamed predators are never scared. A button decides whether your other animals are affected.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text:
The council treats a planter box like a hydroponics basin, so before you have power it may suggest one when a colonist asks for a greenhouse. Give it daylight.
Once Farming Techniques is researched, a grower may wish for a scarecrow from spring to fall, tired of watching the hares eat the crops.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Gauranlen Tree Expanded
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Up to four colonists per Gauranlen tree, replanting, and a ritual to break the bond
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Four of our people tend the same Gauranlen tree now, and it gives us more dryads.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Gauranlen Tree Expanded rewrites how a Gauranlen tree's connection works. Several colonists can share one tree, the tree can be moved, and a new ritual lets a colonist tear their connection when it has to end. A button calls the dryads home to guard the tree for a few hours.

li.heading: Sharing a tree
li.text:
Up to 4 colonists can connect to one tree (a setting), and more connected colonists mean more dryads, up to 1.5 times as many by default. Connect several colonists with good Plants skill so they share the pruning.
Gauranlen trees can be replanted and keep their connections, so plant the tree where you like and move it later if your base grows around it. When a connection has to end, the tear connection ritual ends it, and the colonist who tears it gets -10 mood for 5 days. A button calls all dryads to protect the tree for several hours.

li.heading: Before you add it
li.text: It doesn't work with existing connections: remove all connections and dryads before adding it to a save. It also clashes with other Gauranlen mods.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: The Almanac's base-game Gauranlen pages describe vanilla rules. This mod changes the connection, so check its settings for the numbers in your game.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Vanilla Temperature Expanded
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Central heating and air conditioning, mostly for colonies with power
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Before electricity, the only piece we can use is the wall-mounted vent.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Vanilla Temperature Expanded adds central climate control: air ducts carry heated or cooled air from AC units to the rooms that need it, and compressors keep the network efficient. It also adds heaters, coolers and ceiling fans. Nearly all of it needs electricity, so a medieval colony will barely see it.

li.heading: Before electricity
li.text: The one piece a pre-industrial colony can use is the wall-mounted vent. It needs no power, only Complex Furniture research and 20 steel. Built into a wall, it shares temperature between two rooms, so a fire in one room can heat the next.

li.heading: Once you have power
li.text: AC units, compressors and ducts need HVAC research, which comes after Air Conditioning. Connecting more devices than the compressors support raises the power draw of every device, and efficiency above 100% lowers it, so add compressors as you add devices. Heaters, coolers and ceiling fans need Electricity or Air Conditioning research, and power.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: The council never suggests powered buildings before you have electricity, so these stay out of its advice in a medieval game.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: mining helpers
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Medieval deep mining, ore highlights and salvaging ancient junk
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: The mining bird keeps the mineshaft running without a generator.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Three small mods for getting more out of rock and ruins: a Medieval Overhaul patch that turns deep drilling into medieval mine shafts, a highlight for ore veins, and the ability to take apart every piece of ancient junk.

li.text:
Medieval Overhaul Deep Vein Mining turns the deep drill into a deep vein mineshaft and the ground-penetrating scanner into a prospecting desk, both medieval. They still need a trickle of power, which a "mining bird" provides. The patch also removes gold, silver, plasteel and steel from deep deposits, so Medieval Overhaul's own ores turn up instead. Set up a prospecting desk early to find deep veins, then sink mineshafts on them.
Mine Sight highlights ores while the mine order is selected, and holding Shift designates a whole vein, so one shift-click mines it all.
Dismantle Ancient Junk lets you take apart every piece of an ancient ruin for twice what destroying it gives, including Medieval Overhaul's ruined battering rams and siege towers. Strip the ruins near your base for materials instead of burning them down.
